taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest page states today is Saturday, October 24, 2026, so six days later is Friday, October 30, 2026. The deadline is at 23:59 PT (Pacific Time, UTC-7 in late October). Madrid uses CEST (UTC+2) in October, which is a +9 hour difference from PT. Adding 9 hours to 23:59 PT on Oct 30 gives 08:59 on Oct 31 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest deadline is Monday, November 2, 2026 at 10:00 Los Angeles time (PDT, UTC-7). Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) in late October/early November, for a +8 hour difference. Adding 8 hours to 10:00 gives 18:00 the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on 2026-10-24 at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2). Adding exactly 48 hours brings it to the same time two days later, still on CEST (no DST change occurs in that window).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest starts on 2026-10-26 at 10:00 AM PT (Pacific Time, UTC-7). Adding exactly 72 hours brings it to 2026-10-29 at 10:00 AM PT. Madrid uses CEST (UTC+2) in late October, which is 9 hours ahead of PT, so the deadline is 19:00 local time on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close: 2026-10-31 23:59 ET (which is UTC-4).

Add 36 hours: 2026-11-02 11:59 UTC.

Madrid (CEST, UTC+2 in early November): 13:59 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 13:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 corresponds to 2026-10-01 00:19:00 UTC.  
Tokyo (JST, UTC+9) is 9 hours ahead, so this converts to 2026-10-01 09:19 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-01 09:19

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain uses CEST (UTC+2) in October.

The given deadline is 2026-10-25 at 02:30 UTC, which is 04:30 local time on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25. Pacific Time on that date at 23:59 corresponds to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1, in effect in Madrid in late October) at 07:59 the next morning.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The US ends DST on the first Sunday in November, which in 2026 falls on November 1. That means the deadline is 12:00 noon ET on 2026-11-01.

Peru observes UTC-5 year-round (no DST). Eastern Time on that date is also UTC-5, so the times match exactly.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is December 31, 2026, at 24:00 AoE (Anywhere on Earth), which is equivalent to 2027-01-01 00:00 UTC.  
Tokyo uses JST (UTC+9) with no DST, so this converts to 2027-01-01 09:00 local time.  

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 09:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert 5:00 PM Sydney time (AEDT, UTC+11) on 2026-10-05 to New York time (EDT, UTC-4) during your travel:

Sydney 17:00 on Oct 5 = 06:00 UTC on Oct 5.  
Subtract 4 hours for EDT: 02:00 on Oct 5.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
